correctness.rationale: For \(B>\max_i d_i\), the weights \(B^{j-1}\) separate all degree-\(d_i\) monomials by uniqueness of base-\(B\) expansion, so the product fixed locus consists exactly of monomial systems. A monomial system with no common projective zero must contain a pure power of every variable, because each coordinate point must be avoided as a common zero. With exactly \(n\) monomials in \(n\) variables this forces a bijection between equations and variables, giving precisely \(n!\) fixed points. The converse is immediate. Euler localization gives \(\chi_c(U_{\mathbf d})=n!\), and constructible additivity in the product of projective coefficient spaces gives the resultant-locus formula. The packaged checker independently enumerates monomial systems and coordinate supports on a finite regression grid.

value.rationale: The Macaulay resultant is a central hypersurface of elimination theory and computational algebraic geometry. The theorem gives a closed global topological invariant for every genuinely multivariate square homogeneous system and shows a striking degree-independence: the non-resultant locus always has compactly supported Euler characteristic \(n!\). The value has a natural combinatorial meaning as the number of permutation pure-power systems, and in the all-linear case matches the Weyl-group-size Euler count for ordered projective bases. The result is uniform in all positive degrees and is not a finite slice or a recomputation of a known table.
